description: How two devices' user states merge, and which exchange files are refused. Shared with the mobile client: both implementations must reproduce every case. Omitted in a case: empty collections, peers [], settings { residence: bizkaia, residenceHlc: null }, schemaVersion 1 and deviceName null on the incoming file, and every optional row column (null; fees and taxWithheld "0", fxSource IDENTITY, funding CASH, hedgedToBase false, thesis CORE). An expected plan compares apply and effects only when it lists no conflicts, unless compareApply is true; apply.peers is compared only when the case lists it.

merges.name: Two identical states: nothing to apply
An empty PC receives everything, and is told to fetch prices and rates
The same CSV imported on both sides: no duplicates, whatever the local ids were
The same ledger key with another amount is a conflict
A reward valued from two different price histories is a conflict, not a silent pick
CASH here, IN_KIND there: the entry becomes IN_KIND
IN_KIND here, CASH there: it stays IN_KIND
A complete swap enters with both legs
A swap whose stored leg conflicts brings neither leg
A field changed only there is taken, with its origin's mark
A field changed only here is kept
A field changed on both sides to different values is a conflict
A field changed on both sides to the same value is no conflict
The exposure pair is one field: a new leaf comes with its kind
A device whose clock runs 10 minutes slow still changes a field after the last sync
Echo: a value taken there and changed here since is no conflict
Transitive: C takes from B a change A made, which C had not seen
Two values with no mark that differ are a conflict: nothing says which side changed
A residence with no mark on either side that differs is a conflict
Ingestion fields keep the local value; a missing asset class is filled in
A new quote symbol is taken and its history fetched again
A cleared quote symbol is taken, with nothing to fetch
A target version deleted there and untouched here is deleted here
A target version deleted here does not come back
Two new target versions on the same day are a conflict
A composition replaced only there is taken
A composition replaced on both sides from dated files: the later day wins
A composition replaced on both sides, one undated, is a conflict
The same composition dropped on both sides: a day read from the file beats one inferred
A resolved identity is not replaced by a later miss
A miss is replaced by an earlier resolution
The same resolution with an exchange code beats one without, whatever the dates
Converted rows and rows near midnight are taken exactly as written
